generation.hypothesis: The strength-ductility trade-off in high-entropy alloys can be overcome through the creation of heterogeneous microstructures, such as those achieved through hybrid-rolling or phase-selective recrystallization.
generation.structural_mediator: Heterogeneous microstructure with dual structural-compositional features
generation.mechanism: The creation of heterogeneous microstructures leads to the formation of coherent internal boundaries, which can effectively strengthen the material while maintaining ductility. This is derived from materials-science principles and supported by records judged as transfers or partially.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength-ductility synergy, with potential increases in yield strength and ultimate tensile strength while maintaining or improving elongation to failure.
generation.baseline: Conventional high-entropy alloys with homogeneous microstructures
generation.boundary: The limits of the strength-ductility trade-off in high-entropy alloys, beyond which further improvements in strength or ductility are not possible without compromising the other property.
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms by which heterogeneous microstructures improve strength-ductility synergy are not fully understood and may depend on specific alloy compositions and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of high-entropy alloys with heterogeneous microstructures created through hybrid-rolling or phase-selective recrystallization, compared to conventional alloys with homogeneous microstructures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heterogeneous microstructures do not lead to improved strength-ductility synergy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Question: Can a novel hybrid-rolling process combining cryo-rolling and warm-rolling create a dual structural-compositional heterogeneous microstructure in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy to achieve unprecedented strength-ductility synergy?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA). Processing: Hybrid-rolling consisting of two stages: Stage I cryo-rolling to a true strain of ~1.2 (90% reduction in thickness total) with samples immersed in liquid N2 for 30 minutes before and after each pass; Stage II warm-rolling at 600 °C to a true strain of ~1.2, with specimens held at 600 °C for 20 minutes prior to each of the ten passes and water quenched immediately after every pass.. Own digest: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement.
